issues: Dolphin is rendered as a noisy dithered dot field rather than a solid lit-phosphor silhouette, so the body, fins and tail read as scattered static instead of a coherent creature.
The water/reflection band directly below the dolphin is far too bright, dense and noisy; it competes with the dolphin for the eye and blows past the 15% height budget for subordinate waves.
No clean rim light or defined edge on the dolphin — the outline dissolves into stray pixels, killing the crisp lit-object look the reference demands.
Phosphor glow reads as grainy per-pixel dither rather than a soft OEL bloom with a gentle halo; it looks like static, not lit phosphor.
No perceptible short persistence trail on the dolphin; the dithering creates a foggy/static impression instead of a clean motion afterglow.
Vertical balance is off — the dolphin sits high while the lower half is dominated by the bright water noise, weakening the dolphin -> text -> waves -> FFT hierarchy.
suggestions: Replace the dithered dolphin fill with a solid (or smoothly gradient-shaded) phosphor body plus a crisp 1px rim-light outline so the silhouette (head, dorsal fin, pectoral fin, tail fluke) reads instantly and organically.
Drastically dim and thin the water surface to 2-3 low-contrast wavy lines confined to <=15% of display height, and delete the bright noisy reflection band that currently competes with the dolphin.
Add a real subtle gaussian bloom halo around the dolphin edges instead of per-pixel dither noise, so objects are crisp with a gentle glow rather than speckled.
Implement a true short persistence/afterglow buffer (1-2 frame exponential decay) on moving elements rather than relying on static dither, giving a clean trail without whole-scene smear.
Re-balance the composition so the dolphin occupies the central 50-60% of height and clearly dominates; push track text, waves, FFT and VU/info readouts firmly into low-contrast supporting roles.
Cut overall speckle/noise across the panel — genuine OEL phosphor is smooth and continuous, not a dithered static field; reserve dithering only for soft gradients, not the main subject.
